notes: Contraction paired with physics-replace-0008. Removes the original fact of that revision: every alpha decay emits a helium-4 nucleus. Stored facts only; no indeterminate queries. Definitional removal (an alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus), so results should be sliced as definitional. The derived queries name invented superheavy nuclides (Velorium-291, Kalthorium-286, Drennium-302; 0 corpus hits each, also 0 with helium or proton) that the prompt says undergo alpha decay, so a model cannot hold nuclide-specific decay knowledge independently of the removed rule; they ask whether a lone proton is released, whether a helium nucleus is, and the particle given off (inheritance, 2 hops). Real nuclides were dropped after review (radon-222 and polonium-210 decays are known on their own). Propositional targets follow strong Kleene logic and all become unknown. Near and far queries are kept from the revision (contraction is exempt from Rule 7).
